g1.label: 1. A path can become visible within a few months
g1.why: Paragraph A: a path “can establish itself within a single season” — a season is about three months.

g2.label: 2. Fences and hedges usually stopped people
g2.why: Paragraph B: such measures “occasionally worked”, but “more often” walkers stepped around them — the opposite of “usually”.

g3.label: 3. Barriers cost more than new paths
g3.why: Paragraph B says barriers “had costs of their own” but never compares them with the cost of laying paths.

g4.label: 4. Supporters say paths on worn routes get used
g4.why: Paragraph C: supporters argue the approach “produces paths that are used rather than ignored”.

g5.label: 5. Detroit: more paths appeared than vanished
g5.why: Paragraph D: “far more paths disappeared than were created” between 2010 and 2016.

g6.label: 6. The 2014 experiments took place in national parks
g6.why: Paragraph E mentions national parks, but it does not say where the nine experiments in the review were carried out.

g7.label: 7. Waiting until a site is in use before deciding on paths
g7.why: Paragraph C: leave the lawns “unpaved for its first months of use” and then lay paths along the worn routes.

g8.label: 8. Evidence gathered from the air
g8.why: Paragraph D: the Detroit researchers used “aerial images” — pictures taken from the air.

g9.label: 9. The same action matters more in one setting
g9.why: Paragraph E: a shortcut that “does little harm on a city lawn” may “leave a lasting scar on a mountainside”.

g10.label: 10. People for whom an informal route may be unsuitable
g10.why: Paragraph F: a line that suits commuters “may be unusable for wheelchair users or parents pushing buggies”.

g11.label: 11. a city with much ___ after years of population loss
g11.why: Paragraph D: decline has “left large areas of vacant land” — two words, copied exactly; a longer answer loses the mark.

g12.label: 12. routes linked homes with ___ and with schools
g12.why: Paragraph D: many paths “connected homes to schools and bus stops”, and the summary already names schools; more than two words loses the mark.

g13.label: 13. in protected areas such routes are known as ___
g13.why: Paragraph E: in nature reserves and national parks, informal routes “are often called social trails”; more than two words loses the mark.

g1.label: 1. occasionally worked → never worked
g1.why: “Occasionally worked” means they worked sometimes, so “never worked” contradicts the passage.

g2.label: 2. more than 5,000 → over five thousand
g2.why: “More than 5,000” and “over five thousand” mean the same — only the way the number is written changes.

g3.label: 3. connected homes to schools and bus stops → some paths led to bus stops
g3.why: If many paths connected homes to bus stops, then some paths led to bus stops — the statement agrees.

g4.label: 4. combined the results of nine experiments → more than ten experiments
g4.why: The passage says “nine” experiments, so “more than ten” contradicts it.

g5.label: 5. announced it would pave → paved in 2014
g5.why: The passage gives the 2014 announcement (“would pave”), not whether or when the paving was done.

g6.label: 6. a well-worn track is still dangerous → safe if many people use it
g6.why: The passage says a well-worn track can “still” be dangerous, which contradicts “safe if many people use it”.

g7.label: 7. between 2010 and 2016 → two points six years apart
g7.why: 2016 minus 2010 is six years — the statement is a paraphrase of the dates.

g8.label: 8. plant community a better guide → number of walks the best guide
g8.why: The passage says the type of plant community was a better guide than the number of walks, so the number of walks was not the best guide.

g1.label: 1. decline (paragraph A)
g1.why: Here “many decline” means many people refuse the long official path.

g2.correct: the actions taken to deal with the problem
accept: the actions taken to deal with the problem
g2.label: 2. Such measures (paragraph B)
g2.why: “Measures” are actions taken to deal with a problem — here, the fences, hedges and signs.

g3.label: 3. a growing number of (paragraph C)
g3.why: If a number is growing, it is getting bigger: more and more designers.

g4.label: 4. free information (paragraph C)
g4.why: The paths show how people move without anyone paying for a study — the information costs nothing.

g5.label: 5. benign (paragraph E)
g5.why: “Less benign” means less harmless: outside cities, desire paths can do real damage.

g6.label: 6. reflect (paragraph F)
g6.why: Here “reflect” means show: the paths show the choices of the people who walk a route most often.

g7.label: 7. consensus (IELTS Vocabulary Glossary)
g7.why: A consensus is general agreement — a word from the IELTS Vocabulary Glossary.

g8.label: 8. undermine (IELTS Vocabulary Glossary)
g8.why: To undermine something is to make it weaker, often slowly — from the IELTS Vocabulary Glossary.
